_comment: Ratchet down only — lower a number when a real fix reduces that count. Never raise one to make a red run green (enforced by testBaselineRatchet() against the git HEAD-committed copy of this file, which since cycle 2 stage 8 skips non-numeric keys like this one). Originally measured 2026-09-03 by test/frontend.test.js (Milestone 1, the harness itself). Re-measured cycle 0 stage 5, two steps: (1) htmlValidateErrors 57->49 by deleting the orphan <path> fragment at index.html:15 that broke the <head>/<body> boundary; axeViolations_auth (5, contaminated by a leaked profile panel behind an unclosed modal, and mislabelled since showAuth('login') actually rendered 'welcome') replaced by axeViolations_authWelcome/authLogin (1/1, the real numbers once the surface actually opens A.ui.openPanel(null) first and clicks through to the login form). (2) htmlValidateErrors 49->13 by adding type=button to all 32 static buttons, aria-label to #btn-avatar, role=region/group -> converted to <section>/kept role=group on #race-hud and #radar-dock, and converting #radar-alerts to <section>; #search-results stayed a div[role=listbox] on purpose (real keyboard-driven ARIA combobox, see the comment in index.html). Per plan amendment §5(b), the remaining 13 (7 void-style self-closing tags, 5 no-inline-style, 1 prefer-native-element for the intentional listbox) are lint-preset taste, not defects, and are the new floor for this rule-class metric. Re-measured cycle 2 stage 8: axeViolations_shell/nearby/authWelcome/authLogin 1->0 by converting #radar-dock from div[role=group] to <section aria-label> (a real landmark), the single element responsible for the 'region' violation on all six surfaces; axeViolations_convoy 2->0 and axeViolations_profile 5->0 by giving mkRow()/mkField() (js/ui.js) real accessible-name wiring (aria-labelledby / label-for with never-resetting id counters) instead of a visually-adjacent-but-unassociated label, adding aria-label to the two .dot-color color-swatch inputs (title alone is a weak WCAG fallback), and adding aria-label+aria-pressed to the .emoji-btn rider-insignia and convoy-flag icon pickers (abstract glyphs with no discernible text before this). htmlValidateErrors and detectorWarnings untouched this stage (out of scope — see stage 8 report). Re-measured cycle 2 stage 10 (first CSS-touching stage of the mission): detectorWarnings 37->17. Step 1: raised every font-size below 12px in css/styles.css to a 12px floor (76 declarations), clearing undersized-ui-text (14->0) and tiny-text (1->0); detector 37->22. Step 2: converted the 5 progress-bar fills (.progress i, .vc-meter-fill, .rrisk-fill, .dragy-prog i, .race-row-bar i) from animating width to animating transform:scaleX() (compositor-only, avoids layout thrash — .vc-meter-fill re-renders every 60ms during voice activity), updating all 5 JS writers (js/routing.js:1182, js/ui.js:2572, js/radar.js:593, js/dragy.js:397, js/race.js:362) in the same commit; clearing layout-transition (5->0); detector 22->17. The remaining 17 (dark-glow 6, side-tab 4, codex-grid-background 2, gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow 2, repeating-stripes-gradient 1, clipped-overflow-container 2) are checked-in design-identity decisions, not defects — see css/DESIGN-DECISIONS.md. Two items are visual-verification-pending (no browser on this box, see STATE.md): the .rd-limit span 'LIMIT' caption grew from 8px to 12px and may widen past its 46px min-width badge (acceptable per the improvement directive, min-width not max-width so it grows rather than clips); the .progress i / .dragy-prog i box-shadow glows are horizontally compressed by scaleX(s) at partial fill (reasoned as a subtle delta on a 5-6px bar, not seen). Cycle 57 stage 46 (aspect C, milestone C1): three boot-cost keys added by testBootCost() — bootAssetRequests (index.html + every same-origin script/stylesheet it references), bootAssetGzipBytes (zlib level 9 over those assets plus index.html with its ?v= stamps normalised to cy000, so a stamp bump cannot move it) and bootExternalOrigins (distinct hosts across every <script src>/<link href>, preconnect hints included). Pinned at what the tree measured that stage (46 / 357743 / 5); the cycle-56 improve stage measured the same tree in a real headless Chromium at 46 requests, ~348 KB gzip and 705 ms DOMContentLoaded. Reducing them is plan v1 M7 / aspect E1 (the ui.js split), never a bundler. A Node/zlib upgrade that shifts gzip output by a few bytes is the one legitimate reason to re-measure bootAssetGzipBytes; say so in the stage report if it happens. Cycle 58 stage 50 (aspect C, milestone C2): bootAssetGzipBytes (357743, pinned at the exact measurement with zero headroom) retired for bootAssetGzipBudget = 359424 — the seat-resume client (js/net.js grace window + token echo, js/party.js gate) measured 359345, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (351 KiB). Rule: this budget moves up only with a named, justified retirement written into the stage report and here; the aspect-C target is <= 300 KB, so it is meant to trend DOWN, and the next stage that adds more than the 79 B of headroom must make the same conscious decision again. A retired key never silently reappears higher (testBaselineRatchet skips retired keys; precedent axeViolations_auth -> authWelcome/authLogin, cycle 8). Cycle 60 stage 59 (aspect C, milestone C4a): bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 359424 -> 358400 — deleting the unreachable solo physics from js/sim.js (BUGS.md frontend-003: never reachable since the initial commit, 802 -> 645 lines) took the measurement from 359408 to 357786, so the next whole KiB is 358400 with 614 B of headroom for cycle 61+ (a ratchet-down needs no _raised entry; the retirement rule above still governs any move up). Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 0 improve stage: bootAssetGzipBudget raised 358400 -> 359424, a named, justified move UP per the rule above — two real bug fixes landed in the same stage that legitimately cost bytes: (1) js/mapview.js's init() no longer throws synchronously when MapLibre's CDN script hasn't loaded (it now returns Promise.reject(e) instead), which makes js/app.js:63's crash-report .catch() reachable for the first time — previously dead code for its most likely trigger; (2) js/routing.js's probeTts() moved from a parse-time call (a GET /api/tts/health round-trip on the boot path for an answer nothing needs for minutes) to firing on the first A.store 'route' event, and js/telemetry.js's first flush now waits for window 'load' + an idle tick before arming (T1.4, the mission's first measured boot-path win: verified apiCalls:0 with a working map, see the stage report for why the standard externally-blackholed bench still shows 1-2 — an unrelated, correct side effect of fix (1)). Measured 359121, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (351 KiB) per the existing convention — 303 B of headroom for the next stage. The aspect-C/P-B target (<= 300 KB) is unchanged and still meant to trend down from here. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 2 stage (T1.5a, directive task 4): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 46 -> 45 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 359424 -> 345088 by taking js/data.js (the static vehicle/paint/name/city catalog, 16197 B gzip) off the boot path entirely — index.html no longer has a <script src=js/data.js> tag; js/config.js seeds A.data = A.data || {} so js/ui.js's and js/party.js's parse-time `var D = A.data` capture is never undefined; js/data.js now MUTATES that same object (for..in copy, never reassigns) and sets A.data.loaded = true; A.data.ensure() (js/config.js, cached promise) injects the script lazily, warmed once at load+idle from js/app.js and additionally awaited at the two D-heavy panel entry points (buildProfilePanel's garage branch; buildGaragePage runs only after that await resolves) so a rider who beats the idle warm still gets a populated garage instead of empty dropdowns. Measured 344549, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (337 KiB = 345088) per the existing convention — 539 B of headroom for the next stage. This is the mission's first real byte-budget win (P-B): 359424 -> 345088, -14336 B / -1 request. Target is still <= 300 KB. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 3 stage (task 3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 45 -> 44 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 345088 -> 330752 by taking js/voice.js (walkie-talkie, 15620 B gzip) off the boot path the same way js/data.js left in cycle 2 — index.html no longer has a <script src=js/voice.js> tag; js/config.js's new A.voiceLoader.ensure() (built on the task-1/2 hardened A.util.loadOnce(), which also now retries on a failed load instead of caching a rejected promise forever — the reviewer's cycle-2 finding) lazily injects it; js/app.js warms it once at load+idle (same shape as A.data) and calls A.voice.init() in that .then(); js/voice.js's init() now calls reconcile() once immediately so a late (lazy) init does not ignore a convoy that already formed before the idle warm resolved; js/ui.js's buildVoiceSettings() awaits A.voiceLoader.ensure() (with the same generation-counter + DOM-identity re-entrancy guard as buildProfilePanel's task-2 fix) before rendering, degrading to the capability-stripped section on a failed load exactly as it already did for a voice module that never loaded at all. Measured 330662 (up from the directive's ~328929 estimate by ~1733 B — the extra cost of task 1/2's retry-on-rejection loader and two re-entrancy guards, real correctness fixes bundled into the same stage per the directive's own sequencing, not slippage), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (323 KiB = 330752) per the existing convention — 90 B of headroom for the next stage. Target is still <= 300 KB. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 4 stage (directive task 3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 44 -> 42 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 330752 -> 311296 by taking js/radar.js (Ghost-radar HUD, 15079 B gzip) and js/scanners.js (OpenMHz police-scanner directory, 5722 B gzip) off the boot path together, on a new generic factory (A.lazy.module(key, check), js/config.js) generalising the A.data.ensure()/A.voiceLoader.ensure() shape from cycles 2-3: index.html no longer has <script src=js/radar.js> or <script src=js/scanners.js> tags. js/scanners.js's only entry point (its own self-wired #chip-scan click listener) is unchanged; js/ui.js's init() adds a shim listener on the same chip that loads the module on first tap, runs A.ui.legalGate exactly as the module runs on itself, then removes its own listener so a later tap (after the module has self-wired) does not double-fire the gate. js/radar.js's five entry points (js/ui.js's two Ghost-Mode A.radar.setActive sites, js/native.js's three BLE-detector-alert sites) now go through A.lazy.radar() -- the two js/native.js sites are alerting paths (guardrail 6), so they pull the module in on first alert rather than dropping it via a naive `if (A.radar)` guard, which would have silently broken alerts for a rider who never turned Ghost Mode on. Measured 310725 (assets gzip 304353 + index.html gzip 6372), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (304 KiB = 311296) per the existing convention -- 571 B of headroom for the next stage. This lands P-B's headline metric target (<= 300 KB / 307200 B) within one more small module. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 5 stage (directive tasks 2-3): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 42 -> 40 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 311296 -> 296960 by taking js/race.js (drag-race lobby/HUD client, 6715 B gzip) and js/dragy.js (GPS drag timer, 8513 B gzip) off the boot path on the same A.lazy.module() factory: index.html no longer has <script src=js/race.js> or <script src=js/dragy.js> tags. A.lazy.race (js/config.js) depends on A.lazy.dragy and loads it FIRST -- js/race.js's modeById() falls back to A.racetimer.modeById, which only js/dragy.js ever publishes (js/dragy.js:500), so a race started by a rider who never opened the dragy chip would otherwise resolve no mode and silently never begin (Trap A, closed by test/lazydata.test.js's checkRaceLoadsDragyDependencyTrapA). js/net.js's three inbound race:state/race:invite/race:fix handlers now route through A.lazy.race().then(...).catch(()=>{}) instead of a naive `if (A.race)` guard -- they are alerting/message paths (guardrail 6), so a message that arrives before the module loads pulls it in rather than being silently dropped (test/lazydata.test.js's checkRaceInviteNotDropped, proven RED against the pre-task net.js by git-stash). js/ui.js's 'Challenge to race' button (public profile overlay) used to be gated on A.race already being loaded -- it now renders unconditionally and loads the module on click. A new #chip-dragy shim in js/ui.js's init() mirrors #chip-scan's, written with the fix for a real reviewer MEDIUM found and fixed in the same stage: the #chip-scan shim removed its listener inside the .then() (after the load resolved), so two rapid taps before the load settled both attached a .then() and both fired the legal gate; the fix removes the listener SYNCHRONOUSLY at the top of the handler (before the async chain starts) and only re-attaches it in .catch() so a failed load can still be retried -- applied to both #chip-scan and the new #chip-dragy shim, and proven RED against the pre-fix #chip-scan shim by git-stash (gateCalls=2 before, =1 after). buildProfilePanel()'s existing profileGen-guarded await now covers js/dragy.js too (main view awaits A.lazy.dragy() for renderTimes()'s human mode labels/sort order; garage view still only awaits A.data.ensure(), which is all it ever read) and openProfileOverlay() re-renders the public overlay in place via the existing profileOverlayId guard once js/dragy.js resolves. Measured 296745 (assets gzip 290382 + index.html gzip 6363), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (290 KiB = 296960) per the existing convention -- 215 B of headroom. This is the first cycle bootAssetGzipBudget has measured UNDER the mission's <= 300 KB / 307200 B target (10,240 B of margin at the pin). Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 6 stage (directive tasks 1-3, aspect P-C, first cycle of the mission's second pillar): added infinitePaintAnimations, a new static/deterministic analyzer (testAnimationBudget() in test/frontend.test.js) that parses every @keyframes block and every `animation: ... infinite` declaration in css/styles.css (no browser, brace-balanced parse, proven against an inline regression fixture the same way test/stamp.test.js proves its own rule) and counts how many infinite animations touch a property outside {transform, opacity} -- those are the ones Chrome cannot hand to the compositor and must repaint every frame, forever. Measured 5 on the pre-task tree (hudScan/background-position-y; livePulse+wtPulse+wtChipPulse+detPulse/box-shadow), matching the directive's own count. Converted the two that run with zero user action, continuously, on every rider's screen: hudScan (#hud-scan, the full-viewport mix-blend-mode:screen scanline overlay) moved its repeating gradient onto a ::after sized 81px taller than the viewport (81 = 27 x the gradient's 3px tile, so the loop is seamless -- the old 80px loop distance was not a multiple of 3px and jumped ~1px every 8s) and now animates transform: translate3d() only; livePulse (.dot-live, the header live-status dot) moved its animated box-shadow onto a ::after ring (fixed box-shadow, animates transform: scale() + opacity), copying the codebase's own ringPulse/.m-player .m-ring pattern, and kept the dot's own box-shadow as a static, non-animated glow. wtPulse/.wt-btn.wt-live, wtChipPulse/.member-chip.wt-speaking .u-ava and detPulse/[data-anim=on] .ralert-detector were deliberately left unconverted and documented in css/DESIGN-DECISIONS.md's new 'Animation budget' section: each animates two independently-varying box-shadow layers (inset+outer, or two glows with different alpha AND spread per keyframe), geometry a single transform:scale() ring cannot reproduce pixel-for-pixel without a visual regression this box has no browser to check; all three are alert/transmit-only (zero idle cost on a default quiet screen), so honesty (pin at 3, name the reason) beat forcing a lossy conversion to 0 -- open work for a future stage that can see pixels (STATE.md human item 4). Measured 3, ratcheted from the day's own 5 -- new keys start at their measured value (guardrail 4); this is the first stage where infinitePaintAnimations both appears and immediately ratchets down in the same commit. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 8 stage (directive task 1, priority-(a) bug fix): bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted UP 296960 -> 297984, a named, justified move per the retirement rule above -- js/ui.js's renderConvoy() read D.CONVOY_NAMES synchronously with no guard (js/data.js is lazy since cycle 2's T1.5a), so opening the Convoy panel before the idle warm landed threw a TypeError and left #convoy-body permanently blank; fixed by reusing js/party.js's FALLBACK_CONVOY_NAMES (now exported on A.party, one list, not duplicated) for first paint and self-healing via A.data.ensure().then(re-render) once real data lands, mirroring buildProfilePanel()'s openName re-render guard. Both comments trimmed from the fix's own diff (cycles 6/7's precedent) got it from 297376 down to 297004 (44 B over the old pin); a real correctness fix on a real user path is worth 1024 B on a target that is already 9216 B under the <= 300 KB / 307200 B mission target at the new pin. Measured 297004, rounded UP to the next whole KiB (291 KiB = 297984) per the existing convention -- 980 B of headroom for the next stage. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 13 stage (directive tasks 1-3, aspect P-B): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 40 -> 32 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 297984 -> 289792 by taking the eight default-off HUD instrument modules (js/tripmeter.js, js/gmeter.js, js/weathernow.js, js/battery.js, js/coords.js, js/destarrow.js, js/speedalert.js, js/dimmer.js -- all gated on a js/state.js setting that ships false/0) off the boot path on the same A.lazy.module() factory cycles 2-5 used: index.html no longer <script>-tags any of them. js/app.js's new LAZY_INSTRUMENTS table + wakeInstrument()/wakeLazyInstruments() walk the eight (setting-key, module-key) pairs at boot, waking (lazy-load + init(), exactly once, closure-guarded) any whose setting is already truthy, then a single A.store.on('setting') listener wakes a module the first time its setting later flips truthy -- once loaded, the module's own ST.on('setting') handler takes every subsequent toggle, so the boot-level listener never double-subscribes. js/hud.js's card() gained a RANK table (compass, clock, tripmeter, gmeter, quest, weathernow, battery, coords, destarrow) so a card that loads late (a setting flipped on mid-session, not at boot) still inserts into its stable top-to-bottom rail position via insertBefore() instead of always appending in enable order -- preserves the documented 'card order follows module load order' visual identity (guardrail 6) now that load order and boot order can differ. Measured 288899 (assets gzip 282583 + index.html gzip 6316), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (283 KiB = 289792) per the existing convention -- 893 B of headroom for the next stage. This is the mission's first P-B win since cycle 5 and clears more than half the remaining bootAssetRequests gap to the <= 30 in-loop target (40 -> 32; cycle 14's named follow-up tier -- js/riderarrows.js, js/triplog.js, js/places.js -- takes it the rest of the way). New suite test/lazyinstruments.test.js (41st) proves the RED->GREEN shape; test/frontend.test.js's LAZY_MODULES gate (testRealBootGraphSurfaces) extended from 6 to 14 names. Same stage, task 4 (stretch): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 32 -> 31 and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 289792 -> 286720 by also taking js/tripextras.js (ETA-card weather/share/save, 3044 B gzip) off the boot path -- unlike the eight instruments above it isn't gated on a boolean setting, so js/app.js's new wakeTripextrasOnFirstRouteOrTrip() subscribes A.store.on('route')/('trip') at boot and loads js/tripextras.js (A.lazy.tripextras, js/config.js) the first time either fires, then unsubscribes both listeners. Because the load is async and the triggering event already fired before it resolves, js/tripextras.js's init() now ends with one refresh() call (idempotent: ensureButtons()/paintWx() both check for their own DOM/cache before acting) so the eta-card that caused the wake still gets its widgets. Measured 286509 (assets gzip 280199 + index.html gzip 6310), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (280 KiB = 286720) per the existing convention -- 211 B of headroom. bootAssetRequests is now just 1 above the mission's <= 30 in-loop target (STATE.md); the named event-driven follow-up tier (js/riderarrows.js, js/triplog.js, js/places.js) remains cycle 14's work to close the rest of the gap. Mission 20260903-173653-75d3 cycle 14 stage (directive task 1): bootAssetRequests ratcheted DOWN 31 -> 30 (the mission's <= 30 in-loop target, now MET) and bootAssetGzipBudget ratcheted DOWN 286720 -> 284672 by taking js/riderarrows.js (edge arrows to off-screen convoy riders, 2285 B gzip) off the boot path on the same A.lazy.module() factory -- index.html no longer <script>-tags it. Unlike the eight settings-gated instruments (cycle 13) it has no boolean setting to key off; unlike tripextras (also cycle 13) its trigger is convoy membership, not trip/route activity -- js/app.js's new wakeRiderarrowsOnFirstParty() subscribes A.store.on('party') at boot and loads the module the first time that event fires WITH A.state.party truthy (a leave also emits 'party' with S.party set to null first, so the naive 'first party event' shape used for tripextras would have been wrong here -- checked the value, not just the event). Once woken it unsubscribes and never re-checks; a party resume after reconnect (js/net.js's applyParty()) sets S.party then emits 'party', so it is caught by the same listener with no separate boot-time check needed. riderarrows.js's own init() ends with schedule() (self-painting), so no catch-up refresh() call was needed (unlike tripextras). Measured 284224 (assets gzip 277923 + index.html gzip 6301 -- one fewer <script> tag also shrinks index.html itself), rounded UP to the next whole KiB (278 KiB = 284672) per the existing convention -- 448 B of headroom. test/frontend.test.js's LAZY_MODULES gate (testRealBootGraphSurfaces) extended from fifteen to sixteen names. js/triplog.js and js/places.js remain out of scope (their own future cycle per the roadmap); with bootAssetRequests <= 30 met, P-B's remaining unmet criteria are all outside this loop's reach (STATE.md §4/§6 amended this same stage to say so explicitly rather than leave phantom 'P1 adds the keys' debt on the board).
